name: Dexamethasone
summary: Long-acting corticosteroid with negligible mineralocorticoid activity — short ED courses for croup and asthma, plus antiemetic and neuro-oncology roles.
mechanism: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist with potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive action and essentially no mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) effect.

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Plasma ~3–4 h; long tissue half-life (~36–54 h)
pharmacokinetics.duration: Long-acting; HPA suppression >36 h after repeated dosing

dosing.adult: Asthma exacerbation: 6–8 mg once daily for 1–2 days; antiemetic: 8–12 mg IV before chemotherapy; croup: 0.6 mg/kg single dose; COVID-19 with hypoxia: 6 mg daily

safety.pregnancy: Crosses the placenta; use the lowest effective dose (also used therapeutically for fetal lung maturation)
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; use the lowest effective dose
warnings: Adrenal suppression even after short high-dose courses — taper if used >1–2 weeks
Insomnia and mood changes are common
GI bleeding risk with NSAID co-use
safety.overdose: Short-term excess causes hyperglycemia, insomnia, and mood changes — supportive care; no specific antidote

clinicalPearls: Zero mineralocorticoid activity — no fluid retention at usual doses
Long tissue half-life means 1–2 doses often suffice for croup and asthma exacerbations
good: Rapid, long-acting steroid for short courses in ED and oncology settings
bad: Prolonged use; patients needing mineralocorticoid replacement (adrenal insufficiency — use hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone)

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
